vision.label: Our vision
vision.text: With **Moore’s Law** and the fact “**models with the same capability are decreasing in size many times a year**”[^1], we predict that we’ll be able to run capable agents locally on mass-consumer hardware in a few years. With this, we believe there’s going to be a whole new way to interact with computers and do work, and **Agentic AI UW is building for the future.**
vision.sourceLabel: Xiao et al., “Densing law of LLMs,” Nature Machine Intelligence 7, 1823–1833 (2025)

story.heading: Why does Agentic AI UW exist?

then.label: Then
then.heading: Mainframes to personal computers
then.quote: Computing power grows with the square of cost.
then.body: So bigger, more expensive machines shared between many people were the economical choice. Microprocessors, circuits printed onto silicon layer by layer, broke Grosch’s law.

now.label: Now
now.heading: This moment looks a lot like that one
points: Chat interfaces are today’s command line.
Models running in the cloud with batching are today’s time-shared mainframes.
The GUI for the AI era hasn’t been invented yet.
now.quoteBy: Andrej Karpathy, YC AI Startup School 2025
now.note: We’d add one more: developers know what agents like Codex and Claude Code can do, but most people don’t.

students.label: Who shapes it
students.quote: When a huge paradigm shift happens in an industry, college students like you and me can come in and shape the future.
students.peopleNote: Their ages when they started Apple and Microsoft.

problems.label: What we work on
problems.body: As a club, we’re shaping how people will use computers and do their work. In particular:
items: How can we reimagine agents at the operating system layer?
What changes when agents run locally on personal computers?
How can we bring the power of coding agents to everyone?

points: Gain the skills, experience and judgment that come from building a large project with a team.
Meet like-minded people who could become your cofounders.
Start something from your own work in the club, or from other members’ work.

beyond.title: An alumni community
points: A strong alumni network that stays connected after graduation.
Links between industry, departments, professors, labs, students and clubs.
A reputation as a flagship club: when a company meets someone from this club, they know they’re getting great talent.

items.title: One club, one large-scale project
items.body: We’re the only CS club on campus where the whole club collaborates on one large-scale project.

items.title: An industry-like environment
items.body: Just like a real company, we have product, engineering, research and business teams working together on the same product.

items.title: Real value for people outside the club
items.body: Most project-based clubs build projects for competitions or demos. We’re building something that actually creates value for people outside the club.

items.title: An iterative design process
items.body: Products in the industry usually don’t stop after the first version, so why should student projects? We’re continually trying to improve the system.

items.title: We shoot for the moon
items.body: We’re trying to push the frontier of AI and attempt things that even the industry hasn’t figured out how to solve.

project.title: Hive
project.goal: Have agents that can do **all the tasks a person can do digitally**, with access to **all of their data** on **all their devices**, as if **another you** (or several of you) **is doing the work**.
project.why: Today’s agents only see part of your digital life. A coding agent works on your computer; others work only inside their own virtual machine. So you end up copying and pasting between windows to give them context. Hive should see everything you share with it and act everywhere you can: your computer, your phone and your browser.
project.summary: Hive is the club’s main project: agents with access to all of your digital context that can do any digital task you can, on your computer, phone and browser. Every team builds it together in one GitHub repository.
project.semesterLabel: By the end of this semester
semester: Every team works in one GitHub repository: the browser extensions, the desktop app, the mobile app, the cloud server and the virtual machine agent.
A public website where anyone can download the browser extension, the desktop app and the mobile app.
A first prototype with the basic structure in place, to keep improving next semester.

teams.label: Teams
teams.heading: The teams building Hive
teams.lede: Each team is headed by a board member, and every team works in the same repository. You can join a team any time and sit in on any team’s meeting.

items.name: Hardware Team
items.line: Build a screenless wearable device as a much more convenient physical form of interacting with agents

items.name: Automation Team
items.line: Let agents use your computer, phone and browser the way you do. The PC and Browser teams merged into this one.
goals: A desktop app for Mac and Windows, like Codex, that can also control the real keyboard and mouse.
A mobile app for iOS (Android not decided yet) that can control your phone: touch, swipe and screenshots.
Browser extensions for Chrome and Safari, so agents work in the browser you already use.

items.name: Cloud Team
items.line: Build the server that connects all your devices, an agent that runs on a virtual machine, and the storage behind them.
goals: A cloud server that connects all your devices: the browser extension, the desktop app and the mobile app.
A virtual machine agent, plus connectors to other services.
Storage and retrieval for tools, memories and session history.

items.name: Research Team
items.line: Work out how Hive should fit together and how its agents handle context, and run models on our own hardware.
goals: The overall architecture of Hive, worked out with the Cloud team so no work is repeated.
The agent loop: how an agent retrieves and offloads context while it runs (context engineering).
Local models: run a model on club hardware and serve it as an API or coding agent for everyone in the club.

items.name: Product Design Team
items.line: Design how people use every part of Hive, and test the whole system on real tasks.
goals: The UI and UX for each part of Hive: the desktop app, the mobile app and the browser extension.
Dashboards for the agents’ current tasks, past sessions and stored files, plus custom views for each feature.
Stress-test the whole system with their own tasks and tell the engineering teams what it can’t do yet.

items.name: Business Team
items.line: Outreach, marketing, finance and operations: keeping the club running smoothly.

faq.heading: Questions, answered.
faq.lede: The short version of what the club is, what we build and how to get involved.

items.a: {{club}} is a student organization at the {{university}}, founded in {{founded}}. We build agentic AI products that make a difference in everyday life. We are a community of builders, learners, entrepreneurs and techno optimists, open to every major.

items.q: How big is Agentic AI UW?

items.a: An AI agent doesn’t just answer; it does the work. Ask a chatbot to clean up your files and it will explain how. An agent opens the folder, does it, then checks that it worked. The model underneath can be the same. The difference is the tools and systems it is connected to.
Hive: agents with access to all of your digital context that can do any digital task you can, on your computer, phone and browser. Every team builds it together in one GitHub repository.
The teams building Hive are {{teams_sentence}}. Members can contribute across teams as they learn.

links.label: Book office hours with a team

items.a: A seven-person founding board: {{board_sentence}}. Each board member heads a project team and holds office hours.

items.q: Do I need to be a computer science major or have AI experience?
items.a: No. Every major and every level is welcome, and no prior AI experience is needed. Business and design teams build alongside engineers.

items.q: How do I join Agentic AI UW?
items.a: Book office hours with the head of the team you want to join. You can join any time of year; there is no application, no cutoff and no recruiting season.

items.q: How can a company, professor or researcher work with the club?
items.a: Email {{email}}. We welcome sponsors, companies with a problem worth solving, faculty with an idea and anyone curious about what we build.

items.q: Has Agentic AI UW been in the news?
items.a: Yes. The Daily Cardinal, UW–Madison’s student newspaper, covered the club on September 3, 2026.

items.q: Where can I follow Agentic AI UW?
items.a: On Instagram (@agenticaiuw), LinkedIn (Agentic AI UW) and X (@AgenticAIUW). Day-to-day discussion happens in the club Discord.
